correctness.rationale: The smooth \(\ell_3^2\) Birkhoff--James condition gives a one-dimensional tangent direction, reducing every admissible pair by signed coordinate isometries to one scalar \(t\in[0,1]\) and two orientations. The positive orientation has exactly one global interior maximum: exact resultant/Sturm certificates exclude every other stationary point on both sign subbranches. The negative orientation has one interior minimum and hence is maximized at an endpoint, and an explicit positive-branch witness beats that endpoint. The standalone verifier checks the integer-polynomial root counts, derivative signs, root isolation, and final reconstruction.

value.rationale: The source introducing \(T_{\perp}\) explicitly identifies computation on concrete spaces as unfinished. The real plane \(\ell_3^2\) is the first non-Hilbert smooth classical example where Birkhoff tangency is genuinely asymmetric, so an exact global value supplies a natural benchmark rather than an arbitrary slice. The degree-seventeen critical equation also exhibits the nontrivial algebraic complexity hidden by the source's coarse universal bounds.
